steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C). Grease a 12-cup muffin tin or line with paper muffin cups.
To make the muffins: Stir 2 ¼ cups flour, baking soda, and salt together in a large bowl.

Mix 1 ½ cups brown sugar, buttermilk, 1/2 cup melted butter, egg, and vanilla together in a separate smaller bowl until sugar has dissolved; pour into flour mixture. Sprinkle diced apple on top and stir just until everything is blended. Spoon into the prepared muffin tin, filling the cups to the top.

To make the topping: Stir together 1/2 cup of brown sugar, 1/3 cup flour, and cinnamon in a small bowl. Drizzle in 2 tablespoons of melted butter while tossing with a fork until well blended; sprinkle mixture over the tops of the muffins.
Bake muffins in the preheated oven until the tops of the muffins spring back when lightly pressed, about 25 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Apple Muffins
raw_recipe.description: These tender apple muffins with a sweet and crunchy cinnamon topping are rich, moist, and bursting with apple flavor for a delicious fall treat.

video.description: Watch how to bake a batch of versatile apple muffins that are simple enough for daily breakfast but can also be served as dessert, in place of apple pie.

review.reviewBody: Ohhhhh my...I am so happy to be one of the lucky few who chose to make these muffins as Jan (the submitter) intended, and refrained from any modifications, especially adding all kinds of distracting spices. I agree with Mollytina and her review completely that the wonderful apple flavor just shines through! And the bit of cinnamon in the topping is just the right amount to complement the apples. (No wonder Jan calls these Apple Pie Muffins!) If I had added all that cinnamon and other spices that others thought it was necessary to do, I would have never known what I was missing! These muffins are refreshingly delicious. The recipe stands, in my book, with no corrections necessary and will become a favorite I'll go back to often. Thanks for your wonderful recipe Jan!

these are gorgeous muffins! made em exactly as posted and they taste good, but everyone was right about the spices. ill definitely add a little cinnamon and fresh nutmeg to the batter next time. great recipe

First time making this recipe. I doubled it, as I cut up too many apples. This made 3 dozen large muffins. They are scrumptious. The only thing I did that was not in the recipe was, I tossed my apples with 1-2 tbsp of the flour & a generous amount of cinnamon. Tossing the apples in the flour prevents them from sinking to the bottom of your muffins. These are amazing. Thank you for sharing this recipe, they are definitely a keeper recipe.
I prepared faithfully to recipe except added 1 tsp of cinnamon to the batter and included 1 cup of chopped walnuts. I used 3 chopped small Fuji apples and the result is great, moist muffins.

I bake these whenever I want to make a BIG impression! My version calls for 3 cups of apples instead of 2, and I sprinkle the bottom of each baking cup with a pinch of white sugar before filling them. I usually have to double the streusel recipe to top 24 muffins. they're a big hit!

I have made these twice, the first time I was a bit lazy and didn't measure carefully, etc. and they did not rise and were messy. The second time, I measured carefully, folded ingredients just until moist (17 folds of the spoon for tender muffins - like I learned in Home Ec. in the 70's) and added about 1 tsp. cinnamon to the batter. They were delicous and really tasted a lot like apple pie. If I make them again I would use 1 sweet and 1 tart apple, because I like a bit of zing in my fruit desserts - not all sweetness! Thank you

I had to adjust it for high altitude. I added a few tablespoons of flour, took out a couple tablespoons of sugar, and added almost a third of a cup extra buttermilk. I also needed more butter for the crumble (I ended up using an entire 1/4 cup which is twice as much as it says). It still only needed to cook for 25 minutes.

These muffins are delicious. Only change I made I added chopped pecans to topping and I always cut the butter into the streusel because we like it crispy. I make fruit muffins for us every week and this one is now one of our favorite. It did make 18 reg size muffins

What a treat these muffins were ! This recipe made 12 regular size muffins and 4 mini ones for me.
Hearing about more children and teens suffering from Diabetes, I try to cut the sugar down when baking. 
so, usually for 12 muffin recipe, I use 3/4 cup of sugar. But since this recipe calls for 1 1/2 cup, I used 1 cup instead and the muffins came out plenty sweet. Also I prefer to shred the apples instead of dicing them.
Delicious. Made 48 mini muffins and I cooked them 15 minutes. Only change I added one teaspoon of cinnamon to the batter.

I did make alterations, since I wanted this to be a somewhat healthy breakfast option, but what a great recipe. I'm definitely going to save it to make it as is sometime. I'm sure it would be a crowd pleaser. Fyi, I lowered the sugar to 1C, traded out 1/2 C of the white flour for wheat, and left off the topping, but my kids are still loving it... And they're not the type to have been raised on quinoa or something. I added the 1tsp of cinnamon to the muffin batter, since it wouldn't be in the topping. I recommend taking other users' advice and young the apples to 3C. Made 19. Baked 17 min.
Great easy to follow recipe. Makes 15 good sized muffins not 12. I made no changes to the recipe.
Delicious, but the batter overwhelmed my 12 cup pan. I will make more of them a bit smaller and I will use paper liners next time. But the recipe is great.
It’s very good. It made 18 muffins
Husband cannot stop eating these!
I made these with gluten free one to one King Arthur's flour. Followed directions exactly and they turned out really good. Tom them to a women's group and no one even noticed they were gluten free.
No changes made them just waiting for them to come out they look so 😋

I changed a few things due to necessity- I didn't have buttermilk, so I used vanilla Balkan yogurt, and since it was vanilla I omitted the vanilla extract. I also only had small eggs on hand- I used 2. The result was amazing! Crispy top with a beautifully soft fluffy moist middle, and not too airy or dense. The cinnamon on top was just right to compliment the apples. I do hope someday to try the recipe as is- that sounds amazing as well
Delicious. I’m not a great fan of muffins, these are the exception.

I try to never change recipes the first time I make them but I did this time I did. I made 1/2 the recipe using cake flour (1 cup of flour and 2 T of corn starch), 1 tsp of cinnamon and 1/2 cup of milk and 1 T of lemon juice (in place of buttermilk). Since I had something else baking at 400 degrees, I baked these at 400 degrees for 20 minutes. They were so tender and delicious. Mu husband loved them and he is a harsh critic!
